body.p: The CreatorThe Creator was part of traditional mythology, presented here with a relative clause "who was there". I suggest that this relative clause is not here for identifcation purposes (as if it were a restrictive relative clause) nor even for parenthetical information (as if it were a nonrestrictive relative clause, of which there are no good examples in Seri - I believe that they do not exist), but for discourse purposes, to simply give some importance to this character in the story by slowing down the delivery of information. had given antlers to the cotton-tail rabbit, it is saidThe use of yoque ('it is said') is typical in presentations of legends and certain other material that has been handed down from preceding generations (which may be historical in nature).. Now, while they were quite like mule deer antlers, they were the right size for a cotton-tail. But a cotton-tail typically scurries under a bush when it is running away from something. And so it happened that the cotton-tail did that, and his antlers were snagged in the branches, throwing him on his back, it is said. So while he had been given antlers, they didn't suit him very well, and as a result the Creator removed them, they say.
(This happened to the cotton-tail, not to the jackrabbit.)
